text.p: International Business Machines Corp. reported a better-than-expected first-quarter profit of $1.19 billion and cited a strong increase in North American revenues.
Net income, equal to $2.37 a share, compared with first-quarter earnings of $1.20 billion, or $2.21 a share a year earlier, when IBM had more shares outstanding.

The results beat the consensus Wall Street analyst forecast of $2.28 a share, according to the First Call service. Predictions had ranged from $2.10 to $2.37. Revenues rose 5 percent to $17.3 billion from $16.6 billion in last year's quarter.

The company said strength in fast-growing areas such as services, personal computers and some software offset weakness in mainframes, minicomputers and workstations. It said revenues outside the United States were dragged down by the strong dollar.
IBM stock rose $2.375 to $142.375 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange in anticipation of the Armonk, N.Y.-based computer power's earnings report.

IBM again reported earnings after the stock market closed, a routine it adopted last quarter, to avoid some of the volatility in its stock during its meeting and conference call with analysts, which was to begin at 4:30 p.m. EDT.
